title: JC H2 physics — electromagnetism: fields, flux and induction
subject: science

scenes.caption: Electric field lines run from + to −
scenes.narration: Between two charged plates the field lines run straight from the positive plate to the negative one, evenly spaced. Watch each line draw itself from the top plate to the bottom plate — even spacing means a uniform field, and the probe dot shows the direction a positive charge would be pushed.

scenes.caption: A bar magnet's field loops from N to S
scenes.narration: Outside a bar magnet the field lines leave the north pole, sweep around in loops, and enter the south pole. Watch the probe dot ride each loop from N back to S — the lines never cross and never end in empty space.

scenes.caption: Moving the magnet changes the flux
scenes.narration: Push a magnet towards a coil and the flux threading the coil grows; a voltage appears across the coil only while the flux is changing. Hold the magnet still and the needle falls back to zero — no change in flux, no emf.

shape.explain: Faraday's law: emf = -N times the rate of change of flux. The minus is Lenz's law: it opposes the change.
The key: a faster push means a bigger rate of change, so a bigger emf.

steps.text: An emf appears only while flux changes

scenes.caption: A generator spins the coil in the field
scenes.narration: Spin the coil in the field and the flux through it rises and falls as the coil turns — watch the gauge swing between max and zero. The induced emf alternates with it, kicking the meter left then right: that alternating push is how a generator makes alternating current.

scenes.caption: A common mistake: motion, not position
scenes.narration: A common mistake: an emf flows as long as the magnet sits inside the coil. Watch the meter — while the magnet sits still the needle holds flat, but when the magnet moves out the needle kicks, because only changing flux makes an emf.
